text.p: - Now that China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping is dead, will China steer away from his course?
- Marat Baglai becomes head of Russia's Constitutional Court.
- President Boris Yeltsin's aides did a foolish thing when they stripped a Moscow mass-circulation newspaper correspondent of his accreditation for writing an article the Kremlin did not like.
- The sacking of the head of Moscow FSB branch came as a surprise both to observers and to his own staff.
- China announces six days of mourning after the death of Deng Xiaoping.
- Marat Baglai, new head of the Constitutional Court, says Russia should stick with its current constitution.
- The government is refusing to approve the new penal code until certain amendments are brought into it.
- Russia is living through its worst political crisis since 1991 and state power is up for anyone to grab.
- A number of State Duma deputies have used their position to propel themselves to the upper house of parliament.
- The new penal code to be introduced shortly cuts the number of federal taxes from over 200 to just 30.
